question.problem: Find the principal axes of the curve $19x_1^2-6x_1x_2+11x_2^2 = 20.$
question.worked_solution:
First, consider the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})=19x_1^2-6x_1x_2+11x_2^2.$ The matrix of the form is 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/f408697d4afc249d6dcb4254618cf03e064c400d87e31c8a6c6055ccf9d70d7e.svg)

Notice that $A$ is symmetric. The principal axes of the curve 

$$
\mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = 20
$$

are the vectors that form an orthonormal eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

By solving the characteristic equation $|A-\lambda I| = 0,$ we obtain

$\qquad$ $\lambda_1=20 \quad$ and $\quad \lambda_2=10.$

Let's now find the eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_2=20,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}19 & -3 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ -3 & -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/0442c5fae9cb761b85a9c5be308b79dfc1ff05b379912f0e8d42cb724da947b4.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_2$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_2  \| = \sqrt{10},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/3ff0045c806703fac9f102b44c7e2031c0b5095ac48e122f87947a471f650641.svg)

- For $\lambda_1=10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-10I & =[\begin{aligned}19 & -3 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-10I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/7c8822cb00d532e85b62b4b299b2a2ab47f13928d4ff21bca78413f9df631152.svg) Dividing $\mathbf{v}_1$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v}_1  \| = \sqrt{10},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/ad6348443131aa88232fb0a1d82f7c7ef5fdea6ac5f27addcbe52d891e45b995.svg)

Therefore, the principal axes of our curve are

$\qquad$ ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/5118522a8ac8351d9657f6bf6ed82b838347944141c11fd43977e53ac48b7e24.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14228956/assets/40b663f947e3705fa2a9d2b1fa99634cf76bed6622c11d54bbc7029a40c193d1.svg)
